messages:
alex: Heads up — I see a p99 jump on canary after the recent merge (release/2026.03.15). Baseline p99 ~210ms -> canary p99 ~420ms. Noticed by the runtime perf alert this morning.

ci-bot: CI perf alert: job runtime-canary-perf exceeded threshold. build: https://ci.redwood/runtime/98765 — p99=430ms (threshold 300ms).

maria: I saw that too. The big PR window included changes to kernel selector heuristics + batching tweaks (PR #4523). Could be kernel fallback picking a slower kernel.

jon: Also landed a KV cache eviction tweak around the same time — could be higher miss rate. We should bisect but try to reproduce locally first.

alex: Plan: git bisect between v1.24.2 (good) and HEAD (bad) using our perf harness. Harness command I used before: `eng/runtime/bench/run_end2end.sh --model=gpt-medium --seq=512 --concurrency=8 --measure p99`

sophia: When running the harness add `--kernel-trace` and `--kv-stats` so we get per-step kernel choice and cache hits. Also set `CPU_AFFINITY=2` to be stable.

maria: Can someone make a `git bisect run` wrapper that returns 0/1 based on p99 threshold? Would save manual steps.

jon: I'll sketch it now:
```
#!/bin/bash
set -e
./build.sh
./eng/runtime/bench/run_end2end.sh --model=gpt-medium --seq=512 --concurrency=8 --measure p99 --kernel-trace --kv-stats | tee out
p99=$(grep 'p99' out | awk '{print $2}' | tr -d 'ms')
THRESH=300
if (( $(echo "$p99 < $THRESH" | bc -l) )); then exit 0; else exit 1; fi
```

alex: Nice. Run it inside the same docker image CI uses (`gcr.io/redwood/runtime-perf:stable`) so env is consistent.

ci-bot: Note: canary currently sets `ksel_v2=true` and `ksel.threshold=0.42` in config (seen in job config).

sophia: If the bisect hits a kernel-selector commit, we should test with `--ksel=false` to confirm. Also check whether `batch_window_ms` default changed — a larger window could hide kernel warmups.

maria: Starting the bisect now (PST). Command: `git bisect start && git bisect bad HEAD && git bisect good v1.24.2 && git bisect run ./eng/runtime/scripts/bisect_harness.sh` — will push updates. First few steps take ~20–30m each.

jon: If you get a suspect commit, paste the file + hunk so I can do a quick revert/PR. If it's kernel_selector.cpp or ksel config, I can prepare a temporary rollback.

alex: Also, if p99 stays >350ms on canary we should mark rollout-blocker and consider rolling canary back to previous tag. I'm going to add a note in the release thread.

maria: Update after ~3 bisect runs: narrowed to commits from 2026-03-10..2026-03-14. Early sign points at a change that adjusted `ksel.threshold` and bumped batching window default.

ci-bot: CI rerun attached: https://ci.redwood/runtime/98766 — failing job flagged `ksel_threshold_adjustment` commit 0fa3bce as suspect.

maria: Local confirmation: with `--ksel=false` p99 ~215ms. With `--ksel=true` p99 ~430ms. Kernel trace shows selection switching to `kernel_x64_opt_v1` which is slower for seq=512. KV stats show slightly higher miss rate but not enough to explain full delta.

sophia: OK — looks like the ksel threshold change was too aggressive and picks the bad kernel for mid-length sequences. Action: revert the threshold change on canary, add safer fallback (check per-step latency before switching), and add a perf regression test that exercises seq=512 paths.

alex: I'll open an immediate revert PR to rollback the threshold change on canary and tag it rollout-blocker. Follow-up PR to rework threshold logic + test harness improvements.

jon: If you need a quick patch to guard switching, I can send one after the revert. Also recommend adding a CI perf check that runs the kernel-trace for at least one config so future heuristic flips are caught.

sophia: Adding perf-guard to PR template sounds good. Also suggest documenting `ksel` knobs in the runtime README so oncall can triage faster next time.

alex: Thanks everyone. I'll post the revert PR link here and update the release thread.

maria: Revert PR opened: https://git.redwood/r/runtime/pull/4590 — rolling back `ksel.threshold` change. Monitoring canary after merge.

ci-bot: Canary job after revert: https://ci.redwood/runtime/98770 — p99 back to 218ms.

alex: Verified. Canary p99 back in range. Closing bisect. Follow-ups: add perf test, add safer fallback, README doc, perf-guard in PR template. Great work :tada:
